title: Windows application recovery and Amiga remakes discovery
summary: Add 27 qualified projects from a 36-repository review; retain scope and fidelity caveats.
notes: Root personally searched C64, ZX Spectrum, Amiga, Atari ST, CPC and DOS/Windows. Inspected 35 pinned repository trees and primary documents/source, with one additional repository deferred because a complete tree was unavailable. Qualified entries and explicit deferrals are distinguished. No discovery worker used. Separate original-author remakes, source preservation, subsystem research and unfinished engines; do not infer fidelity from screenshots or a README claim. No upstream software executed. Pinned bytes are ephemeral local review material only; retained submission carries immutable proof identities without source excerpts.

sources.reason: Research-led native recreation of the Dutch v1.01 game. Inspected AI car code cites original addresses and implements difficulty/stage rubber-band tables and longitudinal acceleration in semantic C. Research notes distinguish confidence levels.

Python recreation of the 1992 Windows 3.x puzzle game, explicitly based on BenjaminRi/Banania rather than fresh binary recovery. Inspected engine implements entity types, pushable blocks, keys/doors and per-level step/save state.

Hand-named function maps, provisional names, review tools and load/format research for Windows DWARF.EXE and Saturn boot/overlays. Inspected notes identify DirectDraw/DirectSound imports, overlay bases and sprite/data distinctions.

Inspected Perl parser walks CHIPS.DAT level records and decodes little-endian counts, layers and metadata. Preserved BASIC utility and binary samples accompany it, but no reconstructed game engine is established.

Static-assembly-derived reconstruction with named board, flag, reveal, drawing and windowing logic. Inspected game source still contains variable-role TODOs and suspicious border-loop logic, so author completion claims are not treated as correctness proof.

Matches XP SP1 Spider and separately XP RTM cards.dll. Inspected animation source reproduces effect timing/math; portable core preserves CRT random sequence, rules and save behaviour in a separate 64-bit object.

Early recovery of Windows startup/window routines with matched, partially matched and unmatched assembly sets. Inspected GUI initializer still uses fixed-address globals and provisional function names, and documents unresolved thiscall/object-model handling.

Recovered executable and OREGON32.DLL code with relocation-aware function matching. Inspected message pump defines Win32 message layout, accelerators and modeless-dialog handling. Progress explicitly distinguishes high function coverage from lower instruction/body coverage.

Substantial C++/ATL/WTL recreation and analysis of Sundance and companion modules. Inspected integer-set and capture-session code has real state/collection operations, but external stub classes and unreconstructed-module/parity trackers remain. Reject the headline full/1:1 claim as unproven.

Source recovery split into named ball, board and manager functions. Inspected AddAliveBallToBoard constructs and registers ball objects but retains decompiler-shaped offsets/casts and comments about unresolved class/global definitions.

Native port built from WinFish decompilation and SDL3 PopLib. Reproducible fixup scripts keep framework translations separate from game corrections. Inspected fixes address a fish-growth operator-precedence error in recovered code.

Reconstructed 1995 Windows Colonization with platform/API replacements and semantic save handling. Inspected BuildSaveGameName documents correction of a previously misidentified global, illustrating that relocated-byte matches alone did not prove semantics.

Portable version of facundosterzerforino/legoland, with SDL3 miniwin replacements, plain-C assembly substitutions and explicit optional extensions. Inspected building queue source retains original address annotations and implements construction timing.
Matching-oriented game and configuration-tool recovery. Inspected enemy manager and ending parser use semantic entities, script state and address annotations. Portable variants are separate branches.

Remake of the 1992 public-domain tile-placement game. Inspected controller implements scoring, four-way bonuses, undo/redo, deck and tournament-seed state; tutorial path is disabled and multiplayer work remains marked TODO.

Gravity artillery remake inspired by Amiga Gravity Wars, with mathematics ported through Eric Meyer’s JavaScript version of Grav War. Inspected sprite code models planets, density/mass and missile forces.

Substantive browser fork of b3dgs/lionheart-remake with TeaVM ahead-of-time translation, browser engine backend, reflection registry and WebAssembly sc68 music. Port notes identify Java/JS rounding, iteration and canvas differences that required adaptation.

Port of Mhatxotic’s Lua fan remake with explicit dig, flood, economy and collision systems. Inspected DigSystem preserves named source relationships but deliberately picks up freshly spawned overlapping treasures immediately, differing from the Lua SEARCH behaviour.
Gravity Force-inspired implementation with ships, fuel, enemies, levels and Box2D-style bodies. Inspected gravity actor applies inverse-square forces to physics bodies.
Amiga-inspired modern shooter with scripted enemies, buildings and upgraded weapon classes. Inspected pooled bullet component configures sprite frames, hitboxes, speed and swerving movement.
OpenBOR adaptation of the 2018 Amiga Barbarian Plus remake. Inspected key script maps press/release combinations to actor animations and combat actions; data defines game assets and opponents.

Android artillery recreation with two-player model, per-player angle/state, projectile model, drawing and networking services. Inspected GameModel creates numbered players and notifies listeners of state changes.
Unity reinterpretation with light/dark board pieces, control points and arena combat. Inspected controller creates the initial opposing armies and switches board/battle state.
Author recreates their own C64 BASIC skiing game as a neon browser game. Inspected deterministic simulation drives countdown, course rows, skiing, collisions and distance/bonus scoring.

Readable browser game modules for rooms, hero, guardians, audio and game state. Inspected controller implements piano/title sequence, room entry and game progression rather than a generic Z80 interpreter.
Pure AS3 recreation explicitly inspired by Psion Space Raiders (1982), with own enemy/bullet, shield and sound state. Inspected main class embeds assets and runs a 30fps 640x512 game.
Remake of the Amstrad Action type-in remembered by the author. Inspected game source implements ship momentum, scrolling star fields, collision and exit progression with switchable visual modes.

Root claims complete native 64-bit games, but inspected reconstruction README explicitly says normalized Ghidra scaffold with unresolved hardware/x87/SIMD stubs and 32-bit MSVC output. Defer unsupported completion and source-quality claims.
Published readable tree has only Tauri shell and large minified HTML game bundle; defer until maintainable game source is inspectable. Do not infer full native game reconstruction from marketing.
Physical pinball-playfield CAD replica, not requested game/application software reconstruction.
Unity traffic-light code inspected, but no primary document establishes exact original C64 subject/provenance sufficiently; defer.
Original game implementation is password-encrypted in game.bin. README explicitly says private access only; no source inspection or password bypass attempted.
React/TypeScript prototype has a small creature table and board/UI scaffolding but insufficient evidence of substantial implemented full-game rules. Defer completeness qualification.

Routine-translated JS retains Spectrum guest-memory map, interrupt/timing/display state. This is a mixed source-translation/baked-machine-state case; retain audit-only pending architecture classification rather than assume clean native game recovery.
Cordova package wraps newagebegins/exolon with inherited melonJS gameplay; no substantial independent reconstruction established. Prefer upstream rather than another wrapper entry.
